name: Primary Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO-EORTC Classification for Primary Cutaneous Lymphomas

criteria.description: Presence of persistent, progressive, or recurrent patches, plaques, or tumors on the skin without extracutaneous involvement at diagnosis
Epidermotropic infiltrate of atypical T-lymphocytes with cerebriform nuclei on skin biopsy
T-cell phenotype with loss of pan-T-cell markers (e.g., CD7) and CD4+ predominance
Detection of monoclonal T-cell receptor gene rearrangement in skin lesions
Exclusion of systemic T-cell lymphoma with secondary skin involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Clinical presentation with characteristic skin lesions plus histopathological confirmation of epidermotropic atypical T-cell infiltrate and immunophenotyping consistent with CTCL
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Molecular studies and exclusion of systemic lymphoma support diagnosis but are not always mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Persistent erythematous scaly patches or plaques

common.symptomName: Plaque formation with variable scaling and induration

searchTerms: skin patches lighter or darker than normal
areas of skin with changed color

common.symptomName: Lymphadenopathy localized to regional draining nodes
searchTerms: swollen lymph nodes near affected area

occasional.symptomName: Tumor stage lesions (nodules or tumors on skin)

searchTerms: full body skin redness with scaling
frequent infections due to low immunity
internal organ involvement like lung or liver

rare.symptomName: Peripheral neuropathy secondary to paraneoplastic syndrome
searchTerms: nerve damage causing numbness or pain
nerve symptoms linked to paraneoplastic syndrome

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear may show Sézary cells in advanced stages
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) in aggressive disease
T-cell receptor gene rearrangement demonstrating monoclonality
imaging: CT or PET scans to assess lymph node and visceral involvement
genetic: Loss of pan-T-cell markers (e.g., CD7) on immunophenotyping
other: Skin biopsy showing epidermotropism and Pautrier microabscesses
Flow cytometry of skin or blood samples for immunophenotyping

distinguishingFeatures: Lack of atypical lymphocytes on biopsy
Typical silvery scale and well-demarcated plaques
Absence of monoclonal T-cell receptor rearrangement
Polymorphous inflammatory infiltrate without atypical lymphocytes

redFlags: Rapid progression of skin tumors or nodules
Development of erythroderma with systemic symptoms
Presence of lymphadenopathy or visceral organ involvement
references: Willemze R, Jaffe ES, Burg G, et al. WHO-EORTC classification for cutaneous lymphomas. Blood. 2005;105(10):3768-3785.
Kim YH, Willemze R, Pimpinelli N, et al. TNM classification system for primary cutaneous lymphomas other than mycosis fungoides and Sézary syndrome. Blood. 2007;110(2):479-484.
Guitart J, Pulitzer M, Duvic M. Primary Cutaneous T-Cell Lymphoma: Mycosis Fungoides and Sézary Syndrome. Hematol Oncol Clin North Am. 2019;33(4):695-711.
